events.region: Wayne, WV
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1022 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated between 1.5 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen from thunderstorms earlier this morning. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Additional heavy
rainfall is not expected.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Wayne, Beech Fork State Park, and Lavalette.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Southern Baltimore; Anne Arundel; Southeast Harford
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central and northern Maryland, including the
following areas, in central Maryland, Anne Arundel. In northern
Maryland, Southeast Harford and Southern Baltimore.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM EDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and a few thunderstorms with very heavy rain are
likely through this afternoon. Rainfall rates of 1 to 2
inches per hour may result in localized totals of 2 to 3
inches, which would result in flooding mainly in urban and
poor drainage areas.
- Please visit www.weather.gov/safety/flood for flood safety
and preparedness information.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The combination of hot temperatures and humidity will produce
heat index values between 105 and 110 degrees for several hours
this afternoon into this evening. A few locations may briefly
experience heat index values above 111 degrees.

If spending time outside today, drink plenty of water, wear light
weight and light colored clothing, and take frequent breaks from
the heat. Young children and pets should never be left unattended
in vehicles.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Central Susitna Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Central Susitna Valley.  This includes
the cities of Talkeetna, Trapper Creek, And Petersville.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional rainfall up to 0.5 inches is possible along the
Susitna and Chulitna Basins through Wednesday afternoon.

Talkeetna: The heavy rainfall and drainage from high terrain
near the Alaska Range could be impactful to erosion-prone
areas and low-lying or poor-drainage areas throughout the
rest of the Susitna Valley. Small rivers such as Montana
Creek are expected to rise as well, but not to the level that
occurred in late July.

Petersville Area: Small creeks in and around Petersville such
as Peters Creek and Cache Creek could experience flooding,
with the highest water levels expected through Wednesday
morning.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Western Susitna Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 AM AKDT, The river gauge at the Yentna River at Lake
Creek indicates rises in water levels from heavy rain across
the warned area. Flooding is ongoing. Trees and debris larger
than telephone poles have been observed flowing down the
river. Between 1.0 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of up to 0.5 inch are possible
with higher amounts possible in the upper Yentna Basin.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 3:50am the stage was 22.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: Cresting Wednesday morning above 22 feet.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
